_meta.description: Foreign ownership rules used by the deterministic engine to assess whether a business can achieve 100% foreign ownership on the mainland, and where a free zone remains the safer route.
_meta.disclaimer: Directional only. The 2021 Commercial Companies Law reform allows 100% foreign ownership for most mainland commercial and industrial activities, but each emirate's DED publishes its own 'positive list' and a residual set of strategic-impact activities still require Emirati involvement. Confirm the specific activity against the relevant DED positive list.

free_zone_always_100_percent.explanation: All UAE free zones allow 100% foreign ownership by design. This has always been a core free-zone benefit.
free_zone_always_100_percent.source: UAE free zone company law (standard across zones)

mainland_default_since_2021.explanation: Since the June 2021 Commercial Companies Law reform, most mainland commercial and industrial activities allow 100% foreign ownership with no mandatory Emirati shareholder.
mainland_default_since_2021.source: Federal Decree-Law No. 26 of 2020 amending the Commercial Companies Law (effective 2021)

strategic_activities_still_restricted.explanation: A limited set of strategic-impact activities still require Emirati ownership or a local agent on the mainland. None of the MVP activity buckets fall squarely into these, but sector-specific checks are required for regulated finance, security, and resource sectors.
strategic_activities_still_restricted.source: UAE Cabinet strategic activities list under the 2021 reform

professional_licence_local_service_agent.explanation: Some mainland PROFESSIONAL (civil company) licences historically needed a Local Service Agent (LSA) — an Emirati sponsor paid a flat fee with no equity. Post-reform this is reduced but can still apply to specific professional activities; it does not dilute foreign ownership of profits.
professional_licence_local_service_agent.source: DED professional licence / Local Service Agent guidance
